scope: Time-semantics freeze for the paper and the five result workbooks. No annual model was re-run.

statement.input_sample: A value labelled T in attachments 1, 2 and 4 is the instantaneous sample at T and is assigned to the slot ENDING at T, i.e. slot k covers [k*10min, (k+1)*10min).
statement.model_day: Every problem runs over 00:00-24:00 with 144 slots and 145 state boundaries.
statement.energy_rule: Right-endpoint hold: E_k = P(t_{k+1}) / 6. Declared as an approximation, not as a claim that the attachments provide interval-average power.
statement.template_fill: Positional. Slot k is written to the k-th purchase column. The printed purchase-axis label of that column reads one position later; the official template is left unmodified.
statement.forecast_rule: Attachment 3 hourly forecasts are piecewise-linear in time and integrated exactly onto the same slots, so plan and settlement share one slot grid.

label_evidence.conclusion: Every template battery sheet tiles 00:00-24:00 and pins SOC at 0:00 and 24:00, matching the problem statement. Every purchase axis instead starts at 0:10-0:20, i.e. one position later. The two sheets of the same official file cannot both be literal, so the purchase-axis label text is the inconsistent one.

integration_sensitivity.identity: daily right-hold total minus trapezoid total equals (P(24:00) - P(00:00)) / 12
integration_sensitivity.annual_identity: consecutive days share a midnight, so the daily gaps telescope: the annual gap equals (last day 24:00 sample - first day 00:00 boundary) / 12
integration_sensitivity.first_day_start_rule: 2025-01-01 has no previous day; its 00:00 boundary uses its own 24:00 sample

paper_table_mapping.note: Values are filled positionally. The printed purchase-axis label is one position later.
